Migrate a configuration into a FortiWeb

Copy another FortiWeb's configuration into this one — the whole box, some ADOMs, all but some tables, or picked objects with everything they need — keeping this box's identity, with dummy IPs, a capacity check and a read-back that proves what arrived. Administrator only.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage backups.restore
📍 WhereAppliances → (FortiWeb) → Appliance Actions → Migrate into (URL /appliances/<id>/migrate)

What is it?#

Migrate into copies the configuration of one FortiWeb (the source) into another (the target — the device whose page you are on). You choose how much: everything, some ADOMs, everything except some tables, or only some objects together with what they reference. SATOM builds one configuration for the target, restores it, waits for the reboot and reads it back, and tells you exactly what was copied.

Typical uses: moving a box whose VM licence expired to a new VM, or bringing a set of policies from one box to another.

What does it do?#

  • Source: any other FortiWeb you can see. Use one of its stored backups, or take a fresh one — over REST, or over SSH (show full-configuration) when REST does not answer (an expired VM licence locks REST and leaves SSH up).
  • Domains: a FortiWeb without ADOMs has one domain, root; with ADOMs, one per ADOM. Each source domain goes to a target domain or is not copied. So you can move a box without ADOMs into one ADOM, an ADOM into a box without ADOMs, or several ADOMs pair by pair. Target domains nothing lands in are left as they are.
  • Tables: each table is copied whole, excluded (the target keeps its own), or you pick objects. Picked objects are merged into the target's table, and every object they reference comes along — a server policy brings its virtual server, server pool, web protection profile with its sub-policies, certificate and virtual IP. Copy only the objects I pick here limits a domain to the picks and their dependencies.
  • Global objects are merged, never replaced: other ADOMs of the target use them (a virtual IP, a certificate).
  • Identity stays the target's: hostname, interfaces, routes, DNS, NTP, SNMP, HA, administrators, their certificates and login page, and ADOM mode are never copied, so the target keeps its management address.
  • Dummy virtual IPs (on by default): the copied virtual IPs get addresses from the clone rules (Settings → Clone / Migrate), never one the target already uses; a repeated address takes the next free one of 198.18.0.0/15. Leave it on while the source still answers on the real addresses.
  • Capacity after the migration: the totals the target will hold, against Fortinet's limit and the admin's limit.

Requirements#

  • Two FortiWeb appliances registered in SATOM, the target reachable over REST.
  • A source backup in the vault that is a FortiWeb backup (.zip) or a CLI dump — not a password-protected backup.
  • The target is not an HA cluster.

Permissions#

users.manage and backups.restore — in the seeded profiles, an administrator. The page is on the row that owns the device (on a box with ADOMs registered as several rows, the owning row).

🔑Permission — Without the permission

The Migrate into button is not shown and the URLs answer 403 Forbidden.

How to use#

Preview a migration#

  1. Open the target FortiWeb and click Migrate into.
  2. In 1. Source, choose the source FortiWeb and click Choose. Click Take a fresh backup of … if its vault has none, or none recent.
  3. In 2. Backup to migrate, pick the backup and click Analyze. SATOM reads the target's configuration and shows 3. What to copy with a first proposal (same-named domains paired; one domain on each side paired whatever the names) and the report What the migration copies — DRY RUN.
  4. Adjust the domain map, the tables (copy whole / exclude / pick objects; open objects under a table to tick them), Copy the global configuration too and Dummy virtual IPs, and click Preview / Migrate with Dry run ticked. Repeat until the report is what you want.

Migrate for real#

  1. Untick Dry run, type the target name and click Preview / Migrate.
  2. If the report shows the capacity over the admin's limit, tick Exceed the admin limit (recorded in the audit log). Over the device's own limit the migration cannot be sent.
  3. SATOM takes a backup of the target (the base of the migration and the rollback copy), sends the configuration, waits for the reboot and reads it back. This runs as a job and takes a few minutes.
  4. Result — LIVE MIGRATION shows the device's answer, the reboot, and the Read-back check: verified: 43 objects in 32 configuration tables read back identical · … · 877 of the target's own objects checked.

Reading the report#

Item Meaning
Copied Tables (and entries) written from the source
Kept from the target Tables the target keeps as they are
Identity kept Tables that describe the box; never copied
Excluded Tables you excluded
Brought along Objects a picked object needs, with the object that needs them
Merged Tables where the target's own objects stay beside the copied ones
Dummy IPs Each virtual IP's source and new address
Virtual IPs copied under a new name The target already uses that virtual IP in another ADOM; the copy gets its own (<name>-<adom>) and the copied objects point at it
Conflicts Without dummy IPs, a virtual IP shared with another ADOM of the target: the device keeps one server policy per address and port
Broken references A copied object names an object the target will not have
Not carried by a restore XML Schema, WSDL and gRPC IDL files: a FortiWeb restore drops them; re-create them after the migration
Capacity after the migration Totals per object type against the admin's and the device's limits

Example#

🧪Example — A VM whose licence expired

fwb-old stopped answering REST: its 15-day trial ended. A new VM fwb-new was installed.

  1. On fwb-new, Migrate into, source fwb-old, Take a fresh backup (it comes over SSH).
  2. Analyze: root → root, all tables, dummy IPs on. The report: 882 objects in 71 tables, 50 dummy IPs, no broken references; capacity 50 server policies against the device limit 50.
  3. Live run: verified … read back identical, hostname fwb-new. Point traffic at the new box, then replace the dummy addresses with the real ones.

Result#

  • The audit entry appliance.migrate records the source and its backup, the pre-migration backup, domains, exclusions, picks, dummy IPs, objects, broken references, the device's answer, the mismatches and the outcome: success (everything read back), unverified (the device took it but something differs or could not be read), failure (the device refused it) or refused (nothing was sent: capacity, HA, the target's backup, or a selection that cannot be built).
  • The target's pre-migration backup stays in its vault: restore it from Restore to undo the migration.
  • SATOM's cache of the target is not refreshed automatically; run a Rediscovery.

Troubleshooting#

"Nothing was sent: the migrated configuration holds more objects than … can take"#

Possible causes — The totals after the migration exceed Fortinet's limit for the target (a FortiWeb-VM with 3 GB of RAM takes 50 server policies for the whole box, every ADOM included). The device would drop objects.

Solution — Exclude tables, pick fewer objects, or migrate into a target with more memory.

"the configuration read back differs in N tables"#

Possible causes — The device took the configuration but dropped objects: a limit, a virtual IP shared with another ADOM, or an object the firmware does not accept.

Solution — The result lists every table and object. Restore the pre-migration backup from Restore to undo, fix the selection and migrate again.

"… of the target's own objects lost"#

Possible causes — The device dropped an object of the target the migration did not touch, to make room for a copied one.

Solution — Restore the pre-migration backup; check the capacity table and the conflicts before migrating again.

"the source has no domain …" / "the target has no domain …"#

Solution — Create the ADOM on the target first, or map to an existing domain.

"… is a settings table; it can only be copied whole"#

Solution — Choose copy whole or exclude for that table.

Advanced#

Advanced How the configuration is built

The base is the target's own CLI backup (GET system/maintenance.backupconfiguration?type=cli): its header, its sections (one per domain) and every table the migration does not replace. Each copied table replaces the target's block; picked objects and global objects are merged entry by entry. The result is restored through the same calls as Restore. The read-back compares the copied tables in the source's format (SSH for a CLI dump, REST for a backup), the merged tables by the names they must hold, and every object of the target that was not replaced in the target's own format (REST).
